title: PromotionEvent
description: An append-only, immutable AUDIT record of a single step in the SourceCandidate -> Source Registry promotion workflow. It is first-class sourcing-layer memory (lineage/auditability, architecture section 3/19) and is NOT Evidence, a Claim, a Signal, a BankNeed, or an Opportunity. Records are NEVER updated in place; each step appends a new event. Crash-safe write-ahead pattern (v1 file-based JSONL): a single physical attempt appends, in sequence order, event_status 'intent' (before writes) -> 'source_written' -> 'candidate_written' -> 'committed'; on failure it appends 'rolling_back' (before compensations) -> 'rolled_back' (all compensations succeeded) or 'rollback_failed' (a compensation failed; record left inconsistent -> MANDATORY human reconciliation). All events of one physical attempt share (promotion_attempt_id, attempt_generation); the intent is the event_status='intent' event. promotion_attempt_id is the stable idempotency key reused across retries; attempt_generation increments per retry so each physical attempt pairs 1:1 with its own terminal event. 'sequence' is the authoritative monotonic total order for reconciliation (NOT timestamp). Because the last event of an (attempt_id, generation) names how far the writes got, the log alone determines the correct compensation. The promotion workflow is DETERMINISTIC code, not a Claude reasoning task.

event_id.description: Unique identifier of this audit event (one per appended row).

promotion_attempt_id.description: Stable idempotency key for a promotion of a given candidate; REUSED across retries. Groups all events of all physical attempts of one logical promotion.

attempt_generation.description: Monotonic physical-attempt number within promotion_attempt_id; increments on each retry (first attempt = 1). All events of one physical attempt share (promotion_attempt_id, attempt_generation), so each attempt pairs 1:1 with its own terminal event and unresolved-intent detection is well-defined across retries.

sequence.description: Monotonic global log sequence number. This is the AUTHORITATIVE total order for reconciliation and 'latest state' reconstruction (timestamp is for human audit only and must not be used for ordering).

timestamp.description: When this event was appended (RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 date-time). Human audit only; not an ordering key (use sequence).

actor_type.description: Kind of actor. Promotion transitions are produced by 'workflow' (deterministic code); 'human' for manual actions; 'system' for automated maintenance.

human_actor_id.description: The human on whose authority the workflow acted (e.g. the promoter/reviewer), or null.

workflow_version.description: Version of the promotion workflow that produced this event (for reproducibility/audit).

candidate_id.description: candidate_id of the SourceCandidate this promotion attempt concerns.

action.description: The promotion action. promote_new = mint a new Source; merge_into_existing = append candidate to an existing Source; update_existing = conservative in-place update; reject = candidate rejected, no Source; retire = candidate retired, no Source; deactivate_source = retire/reject cascade deactivating a previously-promoted Source; no_op = already promoted / nothing to do.

target_source_id.description: The Source created/merged/updated/deactivated; null when no Source is involved (reject / retire-without-source / no_op) or not yet minted (an 'intent' event for promote_new). MUST be non-null once event_status reaches source_written/candidate_written/committed for a Source-writing action (enforced below).

event_status.description: Phase/outcome of this event within its physical attempt. Forward path: intent (write-ahead, pre-write) -> source_written -> candidate_written -> committed (writes done + cross-refs verified). Early exits (no writes): gate_failed, awaiting_human, no_op, failed (pre-write failure, nothing to compensate). Rollback path (write-ahead-disciplined): rolling_back (compensation intent, lists PLANNED compensations) -> rolled_back (all compensations succeeded/not_needed) or rollback_failed (a compensation FAILED; record left inconsistent -> mandatory human reconciliation).

gates_evaluated.description: Every validation gate evaluated and its result (architecture section 19: no routine silently skips work). May be empty only for a pure no_op.

safety_overrides.description: Every safety-driven forced value applied (e.g. collection_allowed forced false because legal_status is forbidden). May be empty.

human_review_refs.description: References to human sign-offs (candidate approval, legal/access clearance, merge/update confirmation, registry-field entry, reactivation, segregation-of-duties). May be empty for a normal public source.

before_refs_or_hashes.description: Pre-step lineage snapshot (references and content hashes of the candidate and source before this step's write). Null members where not applicable.

after_refs_or_hashes.description: Post-step lineage snapshot (references and content hashes after this step's write). Reconciliation recomputes on-disk hashes and compares them to the most recent committed event's after_*_hash to detect drift/torn writes (see workflow doc). Null members where not yet written.

failure_reason.description: Reason the attempt failed / is rolling back. MUST be a non-empty string when event_status is 'failed', 'gate_failed', 'rolling_back', 'rolled_back', or 'rollback_failed' (enforced below); null otherwise.

rollback_actions.description: Compensating actions. On 'rolling_back' this lists the PLANNED compensations (result 'pending'); on 'rolled_back'/'rollback_failed' their outcomes. MUST be non-empty for rolling_back/rolled_back/rollback_failed (enforced below); empty otherwise. Each compensating action must be idempotent so re-execution against a partially-compensated state is well-defined.

metadata.description: Optional free-form extension bag. This is the ONLY place additional properties are allowed.
